body_en: Fight rhetorical battles in Yezo's parliament using a hand of argument cards. Battles chain into levels, and your standing carries from one to the next.
See what your opponent plans, spend your energy to play cards, then end your turn. The opponent acts, and you draw a new hand.
Push your support up to the win mark before time runs out. The Floor Debate needs {majority} of {seats} seats. Argue your opponent's support down to nothing and you win at once.
You lose if your gaffe meter fills, if time runs out, or if your own support falls to nothing. Losing costs you standing, and usually ends the level.
There is no race. You answer a set of questions, and your tone is judged after the last one. Skipping a question costs you tone.
Stay at or above the win mark at the end of every turn.
Committees, Town Halls, Caucuses and Floor Debates make you beat several opponents in a row. A committee resets everything between opponents. The others keep your clock running.
Every card costs energy. Unspent energy does not carry over. Ending a turn without playing a card costs you {pass_penalty} energy next turn.
There are six suits of rhetoric. Each room favours some suits and suppresses others. Tap a card to see how this room treats it.
Some cards add to your gaffe meter. Fill it and the debate is lost. The limit changes from room to room, from {gaffe_min} to {gaffe_max}, and is shown on the battle screen.
Guard soaks up attacks, stacks up to {guard_cap}, and carries between turns.
In rooms that ask questions, the invited suit earns a bonus and pleases the organisation asking. A weak answer weakens your card and annoys them.

Constituency support, Reputation, Funds and Party support. Stages move them. If Constituency support gets very low, a Town Hall is forced on you. If Party support hits zero, your Funds stop coming in.
Organisations remember how you treated them. Pleasing one helps you later.
XP buys Rhetoric Training sessions, where you draw a card and decide whether to learn it. Build your deck on the deck screen.
Spend Funds and XP on supplies and hires that help you in a stage or across a whole level.
Office Hours are conversations with visitors. A Floor Vote is a single Yes, No or Abstain decision that changes how parties see you.
The game saves after each stage. Reopen it mid-level and you can resume or abandon the level. A stage in progress starts over.

heading_en: Card numbers change as you play
body_en: The numbers on a card are not fixed. Each time you play a card, every card left in your hand is worked out again for the situation you are now in, so what a card shows is what it will do right now. A card that leaves a boost for your next card raises that next card's gain, this turn only. A card that lowers your next card's cost makes it cheaper, this turn only. Some cards give extra only while your gaffe meter is clean, and others only while you are behind in support, so playing a card that adds a gaffe, or one that pulls you level, can take that extra away from another card. It comes back when the condition does. Cards aimed at one audience give extra only when enough of the room is that audience, and the mix of a room does not change during a stage.

heading_en: Why a card is bigger or smaller
body_en: Two things scale a card's gain and how hard it hits your opponent. The room: each room favours some suits, so a card gets a larger boost in a room that suits its suit and is held back in a room that does not. The question: in rooms that ask questions, a card in the invited suit gets a moderate boost, a middling answer is left as it is, and a poor answer is reduced. Guard, drawing and gaffes are never scaled this way. Tap a card to read, in plain words, how the current room and question are affecting it. A greyed-out card does nothing in this room right now.
